In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aquatic biota of the Yenisey River is a sink for (241)Am. (241)Am is mainly accumulated by suspended particulate matter, diatom algae, and submerged macro-phytes.
diatoms and submerged plants are not the key factors in the accumulation of (241) Am in the Yenisei river system.
the aquatic plants of the Yenisey River are capable of accumulating americium from water, but the contribution of these plants to the total accumulation of americium is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

diatom algae and submerged macrophyte Elodea canandensis can be considered as potential accumulators and bioconcentrators of (241) Am in the Yenisei river. (241)Am concentrations in the Yenisey River were found to be in the range of (0.2-0.8)Bq/kg.
the accumulation of (241) Am by diatoms and macrophytes of the Yenisey River is not a significant pathway for americium transport from the river to higher trophic levels in the aquatic food chain.
the accumulation of americium is not limited to the diatoms, but is a more general process of the aquatic biota of the Yenisey River.
